basis: February 7, 2022 is the earliest qualifying disclosure I could verify. Cerence explicitly forecast $82,000,000–$86,000,000 of consolidated GAAP revenue for fiscal Q2 ending March 31, 2022. The entire range was below $93,728,900, exactly 95% of the prior-year quarter’s $98,662,000. The unresolved issue is whether management had already given a qualifying figure publicly. In particular, the January 11 Needham and January 25 Baird event notices survive, but I could not verify the remarks delivered at either fireside chat.

coverage.detail: November 22, 2021, preceding earnings cycle. Cerence guided to $91 million–$96 million for the quarter ending December 31, 2021 and $400 million–$425 million for FY2022. Neither range establishes a March-quarter ceiling.

The November 22 call transcript also identifies scheduled appearances at Credit Suisse on November 30, Goldman Sachs on December 2 and Raymond James on December 6. I found no explicit March-quarter revenue ceiling in the earnings-call transcript and could not verify complete official recordings or decks for those conference appearances.
December 15 CEO-transition announcement. Cerence reaffirmed the November guidance specifically for fiscal Q1, the December quarter.
January 6 issuer notice scheduled the CEO and CFO for January 11 at 10:00 a.m. Eastern. It directed investors to a webcast and supplied no quarterly forecast.

Needham’s own announcement confirms the January 10–14 conference. It supplied no Cerence session transcript. The conference webcast route https://wsw.com/webcast/needham116/ was inaccessible, as was the attempted ticker route https://wsw.com/webcast/needham116/crnc/. I could not authenticate a Cerence recording at either address.
January 19 issuer notice scheduled the CEO and CFO for January 25 at 9:05 a.m. Eastern and announced a replay. The notice gives no revenue range.
Baird’s February 3 recap confirms the 2022 conference and covers its electric-bicycle panel. The host search yielded no Cerence session audio, full deck or transcript.

The issuer’s published past-event list reaches back to January 2024. The webcast address in the 2022 notices, https://www.cerence.com/investors/events-and-resources, returned 404. An archive lookup at https://archive.org/wayback/available?url=www.cerence.com/investors/events-and-resources&timestamp=20220125 was inaccessible. Neither January session was recovered.

The issuer’s presentation index displayed 2025–2026 materials. The supplied SEC filing inventory also yielded no January conference exhibit. The February 3 Form 8-K covers governance and shareholder voting: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1768267/000119312522026476/d300604d8k.htm.

February 7 Q1 results release. The outlook specifies the quarter ending March 31. The table labels the measure GAAP revenue and gives Q2 low and high values of 82,000 and 86,000 in thousands of dollars. The adjacent $365 million–$385 million range is full-year guidance. The SEC exhibit linked above independently reproduces the quarterly range.
February 7 earnings-call deck. Its Q2 FY2022 guidance slide compares $82 million–$86 million directly with Q2 FY2021 revenue of $98.7 million, rounded.

February 24 notice announced three subsequent CEO fireside chats and gave no updated revenue range. The March 15 CFO appointment filing also supplied no Q2 forecast: https://investors.cerence.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-22-075466/d285364d8k.htm.
May 6 preliminary results put Q2 GAAP revenue at $85,500,000–$86,500,000, still entirely below the cutoff. Cerence expressly attributed the earlier $82 million–$86 million guidance to February 7.

May 10 actual results. The condensed consolidated statements report total revenue of $86,280,000 and $98,662,000 for the three months ended March 31, 2022 and 2021, respectively. Both totals include license, connected services and professional services.

publication_date_evidence: Cerence’s press archive timestamps the Q1 results release February 7, 2022 at 7:30 a.m. EST, matching the February 7 dateline on SEC Exhibit 99.1. This verifies when the $86,000,000 upper bound was public. The earlier conference record remains incomplete. https://investors.cerence.com/news-events/press-releases?page=17
